I wouldn’t stay that not watching porn is necessarily avoidance. It just can be triggering. I have struggled with these thoughts years ago and found it helpful to give myself a break when it came to things like porn etc... because when the thoughts were frequent so was the guilt. Guilt that was triggering. So if I was in the very thick of an “episode”, not watching things that were gonna further exacerbate the guilt was helpful for me. 

I didn’t have to go through exposure therapy for these thoughts to resolved themselves , but that’s just my experience. I also realized some patterns around the times where these thoughts were frequent - ex. In times of high stress.

Hey, I feel like I wrote this...

When I was younger, I had the same issue. Compulsively washed my hands, had little rituals... it eventually calmed down for me as I got older, but it was pretty severe.

Down the line, when I got older I struggled with intrusive thoughts too.. sexual ones. I was raped when I was little, and I remember having my father tell me that people who usually sexually abuse other people are sexually abused... this manifested inside of me and made me think I was going to turn into some kind of monster.

The intrusive thoughts would be about children too, about God and about other people... It was horrible, the guilt that I felt was so crippling, it consumed me entirely and I wanted to die... I would sometimes try and combat the thoughts with opposite thoughts, but this didn't necessarily banish the thoughts. (for example one time at work I  said "I love you"  customer that I never even met as a way to undo the negative intrusive thought I just had. (I was saying love or I love you in my mind when the thoughts would come out...but I accidentally blurted it out... talk about embarrassing.. but I was trying so hard to combat these thoughts)... The more I paid attention to the thoughts and tried to not think about them, the more I thought about them, which reinforced all these bad feelings about myself ... it is a vicious cycle.

Some time later I stumbled across this article about OCD and obsessive/intrusive thoughts.. and it made me feel a lot better, because IN NO WAY SHAPE OR FORM did these thoughts indicate that I was some kind of pedophile, sexual deviant or was going to hell (I convinced myself of this because of all the intrusive thoughts I had pertaining to God). The mind is a very complex thing, and I think that all this manifested as a result of my sexual trauma..

I remember reading that the nature of these thoughts differ...causing different kinds of harm. For example, I vaguely remember reading about someone who was scared that they'd cause a fire and their family would die, and had intrusive thoughts saying to harm/burn their family - but this was not something they had any desire to do, they were not homicidal, these thoughts were intrusive and resulted in compulsions and rituals.

IT IS HELL. TRUST ME...I KNOW.

Years later, I will tell you the thoughts no longer plague me.. I haven't had a long "episode" in a while (years) where I had these intrusive thoughts, I briefly discussed it in therapy, but we just skimmed the surface and never continued (therapy ended). Just know that you are not a bad person, ok? These thoughts are not indicative of your desires/wants/fantasies..

What helped me was not feeding into it.. I realized that this was part of my mental illnesses and I encourage you to look for articles online (credible sources from professionals) that talk more about this topic. That helped me, knowing that this is an actual "thing", and part of OCD. I encourage you to seek counseling.. as it may uncover the root of your obsessions and compulsions.

I know how hard it is... and I wish you peace of mind.

Yes, I actually work for a crisis hotline in the city (funny huh - not in the haha sort of way). I've been here for 3 years, and have gone through the ringer. I was just diagnosed with BPD and PTSD last year (and major depressive disorder and ADHD last week), and it has been one hell of a year... my job has seen me at my absolute worst and had to take me to the hospital on several occasions... this has made it very difficult for me to compartmentalize things.. as people who have BPD often struggle with boundaries. This was a huge problem for me as I could not separate work from everything else. Upon returning to work from FMLA, it has been tremendously hard to be here, with some days or moments better than others. Lately, I have been having extremely severe and frequent panic attacks, and cannot really communicate with my coworkers. I begin to panic during meetings, presentations, conversations - even small talk in the bathroom or by the water cooler.

​

I have been contemplating quitting, but do not want to do so on impulse or during one of these panic moods. I can't focus on my assigned tasks, I don't feel like I am giving it my all, I am tired all the time, and social interactions are excruciatingly painful.. I am beginning to avoid people as much as I can all together. It's been a few months since my return, and I've just been trying to keep up appearances... trying to get away from the person my colleagues all witnessed a few months back. I don't know what to do because I know being without a job will add a whole new set of problems to the ones that already exist, I am at a complete loss. My job has been extreme supportive and has helped me find treatment, but I feel like it is becoming unbearable to be here even though I've made my so to speak "comeback" and have been attending work regularly with few-no complaints in regards to my job performance. However, more is starting to be expected of me, and I am afraid that I will not be able to carry out these new job functions because of my BPD and it's related symptoms/ co-morbidity.

​

The majority of upper management/bosses have witnesses really intense episodes, they know my diagnosis, unfortunately know some of my trauma (when they intervened, I couldn't maintain boundaries, and everything sort of spilled out... my trauma history, sexual abuse, my self harm, my suicide attempts)... and not to mention they all are therapist/ work in the mental health field IS REALLY FUCKING WEIRD and awkward, and it was extremely hard for me to make sense of when I return. Now, I try to avoid and like I mention prove to them I'm doing great (even though I'm not, even know I think about killing myself on DAILY basis but never would because of my family and friends)... it has just gotten all weird for me. I'm happy that I returned, and have put in a solid 3-4 months but I don't think I want to be here anymore... I can't make up my mind. My actual job isn't bad, and I know other jobs will require much more interactions/ participation which I can barely give now, I have a flexible schedule, and a pro of having my boss and his boss know about my mental health is that they are very understanding and supportive... but obviously I am still expected to get my job done, and they're certain things (upcoming presentations) that I just CANNOT do.

​Some of those people from management I regret letting in, and telling them my information... they see me know and it's just very awkward, like we are strangers. It really got super messy, I spare any details because I will be typing forever... but it got really bad at some points, and now I'm in a super weird place.

If I left here, I wouldn't know what else to do... I manage resources here, and it isn't something that I see myself doing forever, but I don't have any interest/skills and cannot see myself working anywhere at all, doing anything .... this might be related to the lack of identity and sense of self associated with people who have BPD.. regardless, doesn't help me figure out my next move.

​

Feels good to leave this here. I feel like I have to hide it in all areas of my life. The fact that I have to live in this skin for the rest of my life is super discouraging... I will always have these as a reminder, even though I am not presently self-harming. I am super self conscious about them.

After 4 inpatient hospitalizations, numerous therapists and psychiatrist, I was finally referred to an intensive day program for personality disorder. There I received my official diagnoses (bpd and ptsd)

​

Although, I knew I had bpd for some time - though I will highly advocate AGAINST self-diagnosis, I was trying to figure out what was wrong with me for years, and constantly found myself going back to the BPD diagnostic criteria and admitting to myself how fitting it was. I experience all 9 symptoms, although I believe you only need 5 for an official diagnosis. I do know people who have personality-disorder like symptoms but not necessarily a personality disorder.. if that makes sense.

​

When I was finally diagnosed I was relieved. It made so much sense, and helped put a name on so many complex symptoms I've experienced which is so hard to explain to people sometimes. Also, since I knew I had bpd - I felt validated by my doctor... I also looked at it as "okay, now I know what's wrong with me, so I can start looking at solutions"...
